text:
Sam K: Heads up - proposing an approach for telemetry obfuscation + audit playbook, want quick feedback. TL;DR: deterministic pseudonymization for user ids, field-level redactors for secrets, encrypt-at-rest + KMS envelope, and per-tenant retention policies. thoughts?
Maria V: sounds good at a high level. quick q: deterministic IDs are useful for joins but increase re-ident risk. whats the threat model and recovery story?
Sam K: threat model = internal debugging and SRE troubleshooting. not intended for external exports. plan: HMAC-with-tenant-key (KMS-wrapped) to create stable pseudonyms. no plaintext mapping stored unless tenant opts into audit-preserve.
Jules: HMAC makes it hard for auditors to map back to real users if legal asks come. do we need an escrow for certain tenants?
SecurityBot: FYI: compliance note — some regulated tenants require original identifier retention for legal holds. we'll need an escrow/workflow if we remove raw ids. :eyes:
Leo P: proposal: two-tier stream. default -> pseudonymized attributes. audit_preserve=true -> store encrypted-original in a separate audit bucket (AES-GCM wrapped with a per-tenant KMS key). access to that bucket is restricted and logged.
Sam K: +1. Implementation idea: main OTEL pipeline does an attribute processor to replace sensitive fields with HMACs. For audit_preserve tenants we add an exporter that seals the original id into an encrypted envelope and sends to the audit store. Only a small set of roles can decrypt.
Maria V: implementation detail: prefer doing this in the collector as a processor so SDKs don't have to change. exporter config can signal whether to send envelopes. also we should document size/cost tradeoffs for keeping the envelopes.
Sam K: agreed — collector processor it is. draft config snippet below for review:
```yaml
processors:
  telemetry_obfuscator:
    fields:
      - user.id
      - user.email
    strategy: hmac
    tenant_key_env: REDWOOD_TENANT_KEY
exporters:
  otlp/audit_store:
    endpoint: s3://redwood-audit-bucket/telemetry
    encrypt_envelopes: true
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      processors: [telemetry_obfuscator]
      exporters: [otlp, otlp/audit_store]
```
Jules: nice. few other items: 1) retroactive access — if we pseudonymize now but later need identities, we must not have destroyed originals; 2) add CI tests that run sample spans through the collector to verify redaction; 3) add rate limits on decrypt ops.
Audrey: strong +1 on retention/retroactive access. my ask: if we store encrypted originals for audit, we must also store an immutable audit trail for decrypt operations (who/why/when). retention for those audit records should be long.
Maria V: I'll start a short playbook doc listing: threat model, per-tenant opt-in flags, key stewardship, decrypt workflow, console UX for auditors, and rollout steps.
Sam K: ownership: eng-platform owns collector changes and rollout; security owns policies and approval flows; infra owns audit storage and key plumbing. rollout plan: feature flag in collector -> enable in dev/staging -> soft enable for 5 pilot tenants -> full rollout. console will need an "Audit Requests" panel for decrypt approvals that ties into SSO & approval workflow.
Leo P: can we reuse existing 'access request' flow in the console? add a new scope 'decrypt.telemetry' and wire approvals to the security oncall.
SecurityBot: Compliance checklist (added): key rotation schedule documented, quarterly access reviews, decrypt audit retention = 7 years, escrow process for legal holds. see https://internal.redwood/compliance/telemetry-audit :link: 
InfraBot: note: exporter throughput/size for envelopes will increase S3 costs. we should prototype size (avg envelope ~ 1.2x original span) and add batching.
Sam K: ok action items: Maria to draft playbook, Sam to write RFC+JIRA, Infra to prototype envelope exporter and cost estimate, Security to define roles & escrow flow. final question: HMAC vs format-preserving encryption for pseudonyms — pros/cons? please react. :thumbsup: :thinking:
